changes.before: Implement canRetry(method,status). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Before retrying, check both the kind of request and the error it received.

before: A retry repeats an operation after a failure. Repeating an operation that creates a new record may duplicate work, so the retry policy must consider the operation as well as the failure.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
This deliberately narrow policy allows only GET with three selected transient gateway/service statuses. It is an application policy, not a list of all retriable HTTP situations.

Read the function call canRetry("GET", 503) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, canRetry runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
A POST creation receives 503. Does this narrow policy automatically retry it? This policy permits GET only. Retrying a write requires a deliberate idempotency design.
after: A retry sends a request again after a failure. Repeating a request that creates a note could create a second note.
Our rule allows only GET requests with status 502, 503, or 504. GET asks to read data. These statuses can signal a temporary problem reaching or using a service.
&& means both conditions must pass. The method must be exactly "GET", and includes must find the numeric status in the list.
Try a different method or status. If either condition fails, canRetry returns false. This is the rule for this exercise, not every possible retry rule.
A POST request can create new data. This helper never automatically retries POST. A real app needs a deliberate way to avoid duplicate work before retrying a write.

changes.before: Runs as a pure JavaScript function in the browser. Passing checks does not establish live HTTP behavior, database durability, concurrency safety, authentication security, queue delivery guarantees, or production readiness.
changes.after: This helper models a narrow application rule. It sends no requests. A real retry system also needs limits on attempts and a delay between them.

project.title: Retry only an eligible operation
